Author: ashdam
Name: Gubal Library
Punchline: Community language localizer. Ships empty -- you bring the language pack.
Description:
THE PLUGIN SHIPS EMPTY. It contains no translations. Installing it changes nothing: until you point it at a language pack, the game reads exactly as it always did.

What it is, is a file redirector. The game keeps its text in Excel sheets inside its archives; this hands it pre-translated copies of those sheets from a folder on your disk, and the game then draws them through its own text pipeline. Your game install is never modified: the archives are untouched and a game patch overwrites nothing.

ON THE NETWORK, precisely. NOTHING IS EVER SENT ANYWHERE -- no telemetry, no analytics, nothing about you or your character, and nothing is translated at runtime. The only outgoing requests are to the pack address YOU typed in: downloading it when you press Install, and afterwards a two-kilobyte check of whether a newer one has been published. Point it at a local zip or a folder and the plugin never touches the network at all.

Because the game does the drawing, coverage is not a list of supported windows. Dialogue, quest journal, cutscene subtitles, speech balloons, menus, item names, tooltips and log messages all come from those sheets, so all of them are covered by whatever the pack has translated. Italics, colour and gender agreement survive, and the engine does its own layout.

YOU BRING THE PACK, and this project does not distribute one. The translations are somebody's separate work. Either use a pack the community has published for your language -- paste the link, press Install, restart -- or build your own: the tooling and the file format are documented in full, so starting from nothing is a real option for any locale.

Two things to know. The pages must be built against the patch you are running; the plugin refuses to serve them otherwise, because serving the previous patch's text would put it on the wrong rows silently. And the game reads its sheets once at startup, so switching a pack on takes effect the next time you start the client, not immediately.

This is a testing build -- please report problems on GitHub.
